detector.robustness:
Method. Each move runs from its first nonzero J to J 0. Each FRONT frame (measured at 19.45 Hz) becomes one detector sample: e is the signed drive edges from field 9, i = 10 x the integer current, and rampDone means |pwm| has reached the move PWM. Moves that end at an end, or at the stall, are padded with 3 s of held count (the host stopped them after 1 s). The firmware's CalibrationEndDetector::sample() is the unmodified repo header, built natively with g++ in krabby-fwtest. There are 10 deterministic variants per move: +5 and +9 tenths (+0.5 and +0.9 count); current lagging or leading the edges by one sample; the drive starting one sample early or late; resampling onto a 50 ms grid; and three sub-frame phase offsets with interpolated edges. There are also 20 random U{0..9} tenth dithers.

Results. All 20 moves give the right class under the nominal reconstruction: ends are accepted, the three host-stopped drives stay none, and the PWM-80 stall is Stuck. No deterministic variant and no random dither flips any verdict. Decision positions move by 0-3 edges at most.

Weak spots.
(1) R2. The hip EXTEND switch (moves 6, 8, 10) is caught only as Stop: the current rises 25-50% just before the switch opens, and the switch's drop has to come after the 3-sample Stop hold. Move 6 decides at exactly 125% (150/120). Shrinking that pre-switch bump by 5% (move 8) or 15% (move 6) turns the verdict into Stuck, which would fail the drive.
(2) Knee curl Stops (moves 2 and 4) fire 13-14 edges and about 1.3 s before the final count. The knee is creeping into a compliant stop, so a Stop-based home sits about 13 edges off the hard limit.
(3) PWM-80 stall probe (move 11). From the full start it is Stuck at 222 (armed, its last forward edge 40 or more samples after arming, so the short-curl Still cannot apply). Starting the replay 59 or more frames later, that is 51 or fewer edges before the final count of 229 (original count 178 or more), it never arms, because the creep runs at or below 4 edges per 200 ms. The documented unarmed curl rule then calls it Still, an accepted end. With 25 or fewer edges left it fires at about k=20, just 7-11 edges into the drive. The boundary sits at the same frame in all 11 variants because it depends on edges only, not current. This is the by-design unarmed behaviour, not the armed short-curl V1 path; on this trace V1's 110-125-edge window was not reproduced.
(4) Short drives 14 and 16 home correctly from every later start: 14 gives Switch down to 65 edges and Still below that, always exactly at the switch count; 16 gives Stop down to 35 edges and Still below that, within 3 edges of the stop.

Caveats. The host ramp (10 PWM steps every 50-60 ms, with pauses) is slower than the firmware ramp (5 every 20 ms). The current is truncated telemetry avgIS, not the firmware's 50 ms boxcar.

detector.summary:
I replayed all 20 FL moves through the repo's CalibrationEndDetector (unmodified header, built natively in Docker): the two start-up presses, ground-truth moves 1-16 and the two home presses. The nominal reconstruction gets every one right, and none of the 10 deterministic or 20 random variants flips a verdict.
- **Knee uncurl (1, 3):** Switch.
- **Knee curl (2, 4):** Stop, but fired about 13 edges before the final count.
- **Hip retract (7, 9, 12, 14):** Switch.
- **Hip extend to its switch (6, 8, 10):** caught as Stop, not Switch (R2). It relies on a small current bump just before the switch opens; on move 6 the current sits exactly at the 125% threshold, and a 5-15% smaller bump makes it Stuck.
- **PWM-80 stall (11):** Stuck at 222, correctly not an end. In the later-start probe it is accepted as Still from every start within 51 edges of the final count (229). That is the unarmed creep rule, since the joint never reaches arming speed, not the armed short-curl V1 path; the boundary is at the same frame in all 11 variants.
- **Short drives (14, 16):** homed correctly from every start: 14 at the switch count, 16 within 3 edges of the stop.
- **Host-stopped drives (5, 13, 15):** none, as they should be.
- **Presses:** Still.

calibration.robustness:
The firmware is the working tree at b11cc9ef, unmodified, built natively in krabby-fwtest; the repo was mounted read-only and git status is unchanged. The full-extend what-if uses a scratch copy of the headers with only CAL_HIP_SWEEP_EDGES changed from 700 to 1500.

The plant answers every drive the firmware starts with this log's own count and current trace for the matching real move, from where the joint is. Every scenario ran under 1152 variants:
- two time bases (de-jittered frame times, and raw host RX times, which arrive in bursts with gaps up to 359 ms);
- firmware loop of 1, 2 or 5 ms;
- 0, 0.5 or 0.9 counts added to the integer-truncated current;
- current held per frame or interpolated;
- the host's ramp as recorded, or compressed to the firmware's 0.52 s;
- four sample phases;
- coast after an in-motion stop on or off;
- short hip returns spliced from rest or played as a trace tail.

Outcome classes (end kind, home, fail) were identical across all variants for every real end. Only numbers moved: the knee's stop home lands 11-15 edges shallow on the de-jittered base and up to 36 on raw timestamps.

Three results are not robust:
- **PWM-80 rerun (11.1):** it flips between a wrong home at 848 and a safe "curled back only" failure on 2 edges of nudge coast. Its nudge-out trace is a PWM-128 proxy.
- **V1 boundary (11.2):** at N = 67 the result flips between by=stuck and by=switch with the current truncation offset.
- **Extend switch (what-if only):** by=stop depends on the current rise before the switch; with it flattened the pass fails stuck mid-stroke.

Limits of the replay:
- The joint moves as recorded under the host's ramp (0.6-1.2 s to full PWM), and telemetry is ~20 Hz integer current.
- When the firmware stops earlier than the host did, the remaining motion is a simple coast model.
- Only the FL leg is covered; leg B's steps are not simulated, so runs are cut once leg A is accepted and the limits reported are the staged values. The firmware saves only after leg B.
- The knee was ~204 edges out during the hip moves, whereas calibration moves the hip with the knee curled.
- There is no PWM-128 mid-stroke stall and no start-from-rest at 841 at PWM 128 in this log.

calibration.summary:
The firmware's own LegCalibration gets every real end in this log right at PWM 128, but the V1 scenario reproduces: after the PWM-80 stall, a rerun at 80 can home the hip mid-stroke, 848 edges from its real switch.

- **Knee curl into its stop (moves 2, 4, 16):** by=stop every time. The fresh-boot home lands 11-15 edges shallower than the pressed-in position on the long curls and 0-3 on the short one, inside the 40-edge tolerance.
- **Knee uncurl to its switch (1, 3):** by=switch at exactly 781, about 0.37 s after the count stops. A leg-A SWEEP stages the knee limits as [-781, 0].
- **Hip curl into its switch (7, 9, 12, 14):** by=switch at out 0, 0.17-0.19 s after the count stops, including the short 109-edge drive. It homes at 0 on a fresh boot and keeps a proven home.
- **Hip sweep (6, 8, 10):** as designed, the firmware stops at 700 edges, coasts to about 709 and stages [0, 700]; it never reaches the extend switch at 1070. With the sweep target raised in a scratch copy, the STOP rule does fire at the real extend switch (by=stop at 1069-1070). That is the right position with the wrong label, and it depends on a 30-40% current rise in the last ~25 edges; with that rise flattened the pass fails "stuck mid-stroke after 1070 edges". R2 stays open.
- **PWM-80 stall as recorded (11):** correctly rejected. The firmware ends by=stuck after 221 edges and fails "FLHL stuck mid-stroke after 221 edges at PWM 80: raise PWM or check load", with no home set.
- **Rerun from the stall point at 80:** press, nudge, return. It either homes the hip at out 848 ("HOME FLHL count=-848") or fails "curled back only 9 edges after its nudge", decided by about 2 edges of nudge coast.
- **V1 window on this trace:** an unhomed hip starting about 2-66 edges out from the stall is homed there (plain stall, or by=switch in one boundary case). From 60-68 edges and beyond it fails stuck, correctly.
- **Rerun at 128/150 (move 12's trace):** homes correctly at 0.

Leg B is not simulated, so the limits are staged values; the firmware saves only after leg B. The rerun's nudge-out is a PWM-128 proxy trace.
